agent.summary:
The anomaly was a feature flag, `kafkaQueueProblems`, set to `on` in the `flagd-config` ConfigMap. That flag overloads the Kafka queue and adds a consumer-side delay, which causes a lag spike. I did not check Kafka lag or the checkout path afterwards, so I haven't confirmed the lag has cleared.

I changed its `defaultVariant` to `off`, applied the ConfigMap, and restarted the `flagd` deployment so it picks up the change. I confirmed the ConfigMap now shows `off`. I did not check that the new `flagd` pod came up cleanly.

All other flags were already `off`. Pods had only just started when I looked. The `ad` pod had restarted once, and its logs didn't show a clear cause. I didn't investigate it further.

`kubectl apply` warned that the ConfigMap lacked the last-applied annotation and patched it automatically. That is harmless.
